title: soup adapters — git for LoRA
description: soup adapters — git for LoRA. diff (per-layer Frobenius + SVD effective rank), merge (linear / TIES / DARE / SVD, pure numpy), blame (dataset-shard planner with budget parsing; its CLI influence scores are synthetic), branch / checkout / branches (named pointers to a LoRA config: checkout re-copies the config only while its SHA-256 still matches; the dataset hash and the base-model id are recorded for provenance). Since v0.76.0 soup adapters check says whether a LoRA adapter saved by the transformers path is trained at all, and soup adapters audit compares what a run recorded with your soup.yaml. New in v0.57.0.

soup adapters — git for LoRA

After 6 weeks of running experiments you have 30 adapter folders and no idea which one to ship. soup adapters (v0.57.0, finished in v0.67.0) treats LoRA adapters as first-class versioned objects.

soup adapters has eighteen subcommands. The table covers the git-for-LoRA set from v0.57 and v0.67 plus soup lock; list, info and compare are the basic inspection commands, arithmetic is v0.71.34, and check and audit are new in v0.76.0 and have their own page.

All adapter math is pure numpy, no torch. .bin adapters are rejected with an actionable "re-save as safetensors" message. See Adapter lifecycle (v0.67) for the v0.67 surfaces.

soup adapters diff

blocks.code: soup adapters diff adapter-a/ adapter-b/ --top-k 10 --format markdown

blocks.html:
For each layer:

  • Frobenius norm of the delta
  • Relative drift (Frobenius / norm of a)
  • SVD effective rank — effective_rank(s) = exp(H(s²/Σs²)) where H is Shannon entropy. Tells you whether a high-rank adapter actually used its rank.

--top-k ranks layers by drift. --format accepts table / json / markdown and routes through render_report_*.

Since v0.77.0 soup adapters diff reads a bfloat16 adapter, widened to float32 exactly, through the same reader as soup adapters check; through v0.76.1 it failed with data type 'bfloat16' not understood (#2058, #2063). It needs NumPy (not PyTorch, and since v0.77.0 not the safetensors package); without NumPy it stops with a Python traceback ending in ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'numpy' (exit 1).

soup adapters merge — 5 strategies

blocks.code:
soup adapters merge a/ b/ c/ -o merged/ \
  --strategy ties --weights 0.4,0.3,0.3 --density 0.7 --seed 0

# v0.67 — evolutionary search over the simplex
soup adapters merge a/ b/ c/ -o merged/ \
  --strategy cmaes --eval ./tasks.jsonl --budget 1h

blocks.html:
Strategies:

  • linear — weighted average. Baseline.
  • ties (Yadav et al. 2023) — trim by density → elect majority sign → disjoint average. Tied-sign defaults to +1.
  • dare (Yu et al. 2024) — Bernoulli drop with density, rescale by 1/density, deterministic via --seed.
  • svd — linear-merge then low-rank SVD reconstruction (--rank).
  • cmaes (v0.67, Sakana-style) — rank-mu CMA-ES (pure Python, no cma dep) over N-1 softmaxed logits on the simplex. Population [2..256], generations [1..10K], plateau-detects after 3 no-improvement gens. An eval-fn failure scores a sentinel so one broken eval does not crash the run; since v0.77.0 a search in which every evaluation failed stops instead (below).

--eval must be a .jsonl file of eval tasks: one JSON object per line with a prompt and optionally expected, scoring and category, the same file soup eval custom --tasks reads. A .yaml suite is not read; since v0.77.0 the "requires --eval" error text says so (path to a .jsonl eval suite; the loader accepts .jsonl only), where through v0.76.1 it said "YAML/JSONL". Any failure while scoring a candidate (an unreadable suite, or a base model that fails to load) scores -1e9 instead of stopping the run. Since v0.77.0 a search in which every evaluation failed exits 2 and writes no adapter (#1808, #1905), with cmaes merge failed: every evaluation failed: N evaluation(s) over M generation(s), none returned a finite score. First failure: ... No merge is written; fix the eval suite or the scorer and run again. Through v0.76.1 that case wrote a "converged" merge built from the first random sample and exited 0, with a Best score of -1000000000.0000 in the final panel. A search where only some candidates failed still finishes, so check the Best score line before you use the result.

Re-run this. A soup adapters merge --strategy cmaes run from before v0.77.0 whose final panel's Best score: line read -1000000000.0000 had no evaluation that returned a score: the merge it wrote was the first random sample's weighting, not a search result (#1905). Fix the eval suite and run the merge again.

Live as of v0.71.4 — --canary <canary.json> scores the merged adapter OK/MINOR/MAJOR via the Quant-Lobotomy taxonomy (--strict-verdict exits 2 on MAJOR), and --strategy cmaes runs the full evolutionary eval-suite loop (merge → materialise → score → write best). The canary file holds precomputed scores shaped {"baseline_scores": [...], "candidate_scores": [...]}, not an eval suite, and --canary and --strict-verdict are refused with --strategy cmaes (exit 2): the --eval suite already drives that search. The backdoor-scan + license-conflict gates run for every strategy.

soup adapters blame — dataset-row attribution (the plan is real, the CLI scores are not)

blocks.code: soup adapters blame adapter/ --dataset eval.jsonl --layer q_proj.7 --budget 5m --shards 4 --plan-only

blocks.html:
The plan half is real. It splits the dataset into --shards hold-out ranges (2 to 100) and checks they fit a wall-clock budget. parse_budget accepts 60s / 5m / 2h (bounds [60s, 24h], default 4h). _MIN_PER_SHARD_SECONDS = 30 checks feasibility, so if the budget can't cover shards × 30s the plan is reported infeasible and nothing runs. It returns a frozen BlamePlan with one BlameShardWork per shard, and --plan-only prints it and stops.

Without --plan-only the command goes on to print a ranked influence table (--top-k rows, 1 to 10,000, default 50; -o also writes JSON). At v0.77.0 that table is not measured from your adapter (the blame code is unchanged since v0.76.0). The v0.66.0 runner implements a DataInf-style influence score (cosine of a row gradient against a probe gradient, times the row norm) and takes a caller-supplied probe function that returns real per-row gradients, but the CLI never passes one. With no probe function the runner falls back to a deterministic synthetic probe: random per-row vectors seeded from the adapter path, dataset path and --layer string. The adapter is never opened and the dataset is only counted, so the run finishes in a fraction of a second, and an adapter directory that does not exist still prints a table and exits 0. Use the row_id and influence columns as placeholders, not as evidence about your data. --layer is a label recorded in the output (up to 256 characters), not a selector.

soup adapters branch — named, SHA-pinned configs

blocks.code: soup adapters branch chat-llama-v3 -c soup.yaml --base meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B --dataset data.jsonl

name              chat-llama-v3
config_path       soup.yaml
config_sha256     a3f1...
dataset_sha256    7c92...
base_model        meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B
created_at        2026-05-15T23:14:02Z
soup_version      0.58.0

blocks.html:
Branch-name regex: ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._\-]{0,127}$. Config files capped at 1 MiB. Pointer file capped at 1,024 entries. Atomic write + POSIX 0o600. SOUP_BRANCHES_DIR env override containment-checked to $HOME / $CWD / $TMPDIR.

soup adapters checkout — copy the branch's config back out

Copies the config file the branch points at to -o, but only if that file still hashes to the recorded config_sha256. A branch stores a pointer and hashes, not a copy of the config. Edit soup.yaml after making the branch and checkout exits 2 with branch config drifted from snapshot SHA, and because the original contents were never stored, the earlier version cannot be restored from the branch at all: keep a copy or a commit of any config you may want back. The dataset hash is recorded for provenance but is not re-checked, so editing the dataset does not make checkout fail.
